blocks.prompt: 9. Find the sum to \(n\) terms of the series: \(\frac{2n + 1}{2n - 1} + 3\left(\frac{2n + 1}{2n - 1}\right)^{2} + 5\left(\frac{2n + 1}{2n - 1}\right)^{3} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
An A.G.P. whose ratio is the fraction \(\frac{2n+1}{2n-1}\); \(n\) appears both in the ratio and as the number of terms.
To keep the working short call the ratio \(y\); the A.P. part is \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\).
Plan: two helpful facts about \(y\), then multiply by \(y\), shift, subtract, sum the G.P., simplify, put \(y\) back.
steps:
Given: \(y + 3y^{2} + 5y^{3} + \cdots\) (\(n\) terms) with \(y = \frac{2n+1}{2n-1}\); A.P. \(1, 3, 5, \ldots\), G.P. ratio \(y\)
To find: \(S\), the sum of \(n\) terms.
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum. Since \(n\) is already used, the counter in the \(k\)th term is \(k\): \(T_k = (2k - 1)y^{k}\).

Two helpful facts
\[1 - y = \dfrac{(2n - 1) - (2n + 1)}{2n - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2}{2n - 1}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{1 - y} = -\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}\]
\[(2n - 1)y = 2n + 1\]
Why: We will divide by \(1 - y\) and meet \((2n - 1)y\); both become simple.

Write \(S\) and \(yS\)
\[S = y + 3y^{2} + 5y^{3} + \cdots + (2n - 1)y^{n}\]
\[yS = y^{2} + 3y^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (2n - 3)y^{n} + (2n - 1)y^{n+1}\]
Why: Multiply by \(y\) and shift one place so equal powers line up.

Subtract
\[(1 - y)S = y + 2y^{2} + 2y^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + 2y^{n} - (2n - 1)y^{n+1}\]
\[= y + 2(y^{2} + \cdots + y^{n})\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)y^{n+1}\]
Why: Each pair leaves 2 times the power, e.g. \((3 - 1)y^2 = 2y^2\); the first term \(y\) stays; the last term is subtracted.

Put it back and simplify
\[(1 - y)S = y + (2n - 1)y^{n+1}\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)y^{2} - (2n - 1)y^{n+1}\]
\[= y - (2n - 1)y^{2}\]
\[= y[1 - (2n - 1)y]\]
\[= y[1 - (2n + 1)] = -2n\,y\]
Why: The \(y^{n+1}\) terms cancel; take \(y\) common and use \((2n - 1)y = 2n + 1\).

Divide by \(1 - y\) and put back \(y\)
\[S = -2n\,y \cdot \dfrac{1}{1 - y}\]
\[= -2n\,y\left(-\dfrac{2n - 1}{2}\right)\]
\[= n(2n - 1)y\]
\[= n(2n - 1) \cdot \dfrac{2n + 1}{2n - 1}\]
\[= n(2n + 1)\]
Why: Dividing by \(1 - y\) is multiplying by \(-\frac{2n - 1}{2}\); minus times minus is plus; \(2n - 1\) cancels.

Check with \(n = 1\) and \(n = 2\)
\[n = 1:\ y = 3,\ S = 3 = 1(3) \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ y = \tfrac{5}{3},\ \tfrac{5}{3} + 3 \cdot \tfrac{25}{9} = 10\]
\[2(5) = 10 \;\checkmark\]
Why: For \(n = 1\) the series has one term \(y = 3\); for \(n = 2\), \(y = \frac53\) and two terms.
